methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $100M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ocean Infinity, a growth-stage maritime technology company founded by Oliver Plunkett, has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a narrow comparable universe: one identified private peer (Orbital Marine Power) and no public comparables in the ocean and maritime technology sector, reflecting the early-stage maturity and fragmentation of this market.

The stage-progression method, the sole applicable triangulation approach given data constraints, applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $100M+ total capital raised as a baseline valuation proxy. This methodology yields an implied valuation of $120M, consistent with typical Growth-stage step-up dynamics observed in venture progression. The triangulated range derived from this single-method framework spans $102M (low) to $138M (high), with a median of $120M.

The narrow methodological aperture and minimal comparable set introduce material uncertainty into this valuation range. The absence of public market comps and limited private peer data preclude revenue multiple, exit multiple, or discounted cash flow corroboration. Any refinement would require additional data on Ocean Infinity's revenue trajectory, capital efficiency, and margin profile, as well as expanded comparable set construction. The $102M–$138M range should therefore be treated as preliminary pending fuller market and operational context.
